# sec-filing-ingestion — Roadmap

## Outcomes

Source: your partner's words, 2026-11-06 ("the quarterly and daily index files first, then the individual submissions, then 10-K and 8-K handling"; ranked in that order, one track, known progression). Background: specs/sec-filing-index-ingestion-spec.md, specs/sec-filing-index-ingestion-adr.md.
Choices made: Python 3.14 (`.python-version`). A uv workspace of four packages: sec-edgar-client, sec-edgar-download, sec-edgar-index-ingest, sec-edgar-ingest (root `pyproject.toml`). The ADR's Azure platform is Proposed, not chosen.

| # | Outcome | Track | Rank | Cost (estimate; basis) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| O1 | The quarterly and daily index files, ingested into one filing-index table | A | 1 | Small: about 135 quarterly files since 1993 plus one daily file per business day, minutes of downloading at 3 requests/second (SEC full-index and daily-index directories, spec §4.8 rate). Measured by Stage 1 |
| O2 | The individual submissions that the index rows name, downloaded | A | 2 | Large: millions of files, weeks for the full history at 3 requests/second (index row count × request rate). Not yet measured |
| O3 | 10-K and 8-K filings picked out of the submissions, with their main documents extracted | A | 3 | Unknown until the submissions are on disk |

Tracks: A — SEC filing ingestion (known progression).

## Stages

- [ ] Stage 1: Filing-index table
      Objective: Ingest real quarterly and daily index files into one filing-index table.
      Outcomes: O1
      Consumes: nothing (package scaffolds only)
      Produces: a filing-index table built from real index files, which Stage 2 reads to name submissions; specs/sec-filing-ingestion-stage-1-findings.md
      Exit: O1: the table holds the rows of the real quarterly and daily index files for the range ingested, with row counts per quarter reported. Measured cost of the real run (elapsed time, bytes downloaded, requests made, peak request rate) is recorded in the findings file.
      Leaves out: manifests and traceability (Stage 4); point-in-time awareness (Stage 5); full validation suites (Stage 6); scheduling and deployment (Stage 7)
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 2: Submission download
      Objective: Download the submissions that the filing-index rows name.
      Outcomes: O2
      Consumes: Stage 1's filing-index table
      Produces: submissions on disk, each findable from its index row, which Stage 3 reads
      Exit: O2: the submissions named by the index rows of the range downloaded are on disk, with any missing or failed ones counted and listed. Time and bytes per 1,000 submissions are recorded, for sizing the full history.
      Leaves out: manifests and traceability (Stage 4); point-in-time awareness (Stage 5); full validation suites (Stage 6); scheduling and deployment (Stage 7)
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 3: 10-K and 8-K handling
      Objective: Pick 10-K and 8-K filings out of the downloaded submissions and extract their main documents.
      Outcomes: O3
      Consumes: Stage 2's downloaded submissions
      Produces: extracted main documents for 10-K and 8-K filings, each linked to its submission
      Exit: O3: for the submissions on disk, every 10-K and 8-K is identified, and its main document is extracted or listed as failed with a reason.
      Leaves out: manifests and traceability (Stage 4); point-in-time awareness (Stage 5); full validation suites (Stage 6); scheduling and deployment (Stage 7)
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 4: Manifests and traceability
      Objective: Make every index row, submission and extracted document traceable to the source bytes it came from, and replayable without a new download.
      Outcomes: O1, O2, O3 (hardening)
      Consumes: Stages 1–3 outputs
      Produces: manifests and traceability over all three outputs, which Stages 5–7 rely on
      Exit: O1: each index row names its source file and hash. O2: each submission names its source and hash. O3: each extracted document names its submission. A re-run from retained bytes reproduces each output with no SEC requests.
      Leaves out: point-in-time awareness (Stage 5); full validation suites (Stage 6); scheduling and deployment (Stage 7)
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 5: Point-in-time awareness
      Objective: Keep earlier versions readable when the SEC revises the quarterly indexes, and make the table's state at a past date recoverable.
      Outcomes: O1, O2, O3 (hardening)
      Consumes: Stage 4's manifests and traceability
      Produces: versioned filing-index state with recorded changes, which Stages 6–7 rely on
      Exit: O1: re-reading a revised quarterly index records its additions, changes and removals, and the prior version stays readable. O2 and O3: submissions and documents tied to a changed or removed row are flagged, not silently dropped.
      Leaves out: full validation suites (Stage 6); scheduling and deployment (Stage 7)
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 6: Full validation suites
      Objective: Cover the historical formats and failure paths of all three outputs with committed fixtures and mocked SEC responses.
      Outcomes: O1, O2, O3 (hardening)
      Consumes: Stages 1–5 outputs
      Produces: a CI suite that downloads nothing from the SEC, which Stage 7 gates deployment on
      Exit: O1, O2 and O3: CI passes on fixtures that span the ingested range's index and submission formats, plus malformed, truncated and HTML-error inputs, which fail closed.
      Leaves out: scheduling and deployment (Stage 7)
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 7: Scheduling and deployment
      Objective: Run daily ingestion, catch-up after missed runs, and periodic quarterly re-reads on a schedule in a deployed environment.
      Outcomes: O1, O2, O3 (hardening)
      Consumes: Stage 6's CI suite; Stages 4–5 outputs
      Produces: a deployed, scheduled pipeline with run reports and alerts
      Exit: O1, O2 and O3: observed scheduled runs (not manual ones) ingest new index files and their submissions and documents, a deliberately missed run catches up, and failures raise alerts.
      Leaves out: nothing
      ROUTING: brainstorming

## Stage-spec stamp

Every stage spec's Rollout note carries this line, which writing-plans then copies verbatim into the stage plan's header:

> stage and re-validate later stages against what shipped.

## Completion

When every stage is ticked, re-run the gap rubric (derive-roadmap §6) over O1–O3. Each verdict must cite a path:line or a test name and the stage plan that built it; a stage stamp alone is not evidence. An unmet outcome exits as a new stage or a written deferral.
